messages:
marta: ran the initial bringup for the new embed model (sparrow-small-vec) + int8 per-channel. quick summary: overall recall@10 looks fine on en->en, but FR/JP hang on paraphrase pairs — recall@10 down ~9% and cluster silhouette drops 0.12. weirdly density in the center increased, paraphrases collapse together with unrelated short queries :thinking:

kevin: can you paste the eval command and a tiny sample of the failing pairs? curious if it's a normalization mismatch or cosine shift after quantization. also: did you try cosine vs dot?

marta: sure. eval command:
```
./eval_embeddings.py --model sparrow-small-vec --quant int8 --dataset multilingual-paraphrase-subset --metric recall@10,si,cos_shift --samples 2000
```
example failing pair (fr):
- "quel est le prix du billet"
- "combien coûte un ticket"
cosine(original) = 0.88, cosine(quant) = 0.61

josh: 0.61 is a huge delta. that smells like either per-tile rounding bias or missing final L2 norm post-quant. we had a similar thing with the older prod model when we forgot renorm after PQ. can you check norms distribution?

marta: norms histogram attached (pasted numbers): before quant mean 1.002 sd 0.03, after quant mean 0.82 sd 0.25. so renorm definitely changed.

li: if renorm is off then comparing cosine is noisy. two quick experiments: 1) force L2 renorm after dequant and re-eval, 2) evaluate with euclidean ranking (L2) as a sanity check. also try rotational alignment (Procrustes) between float and dequanted vectors to see systematic rotation.

kevin: also try blending an alignment loss during offline calibration. small trick: when we calibrate int8, add a tiny MSE term to the contrastive loss to preserve orientation. alpha ~0.02 helped before.

marta: good call. I'll run three runs this afternoon: A) add L2 renorm post-dequant, B) Procrustes align float->quant and measure cos_shift, C) retrain small calibration with loss_blend alpha=0.02.

eva: for FR/JP specifically, generate synthetic anchors by back-translation and transliteration to expand paraphrase coverage. often recall drop is worse on low-diversity anchor sets. i can spin up a 5k synthetic pair set if you want.

marta: please do, @eva. that will cover idiomatic rewrites we don't have.

josh: also compute per-token-length stratified recall@10. short queries (<6 tokens) are usually the noise sink. include short-only and long-only buckets.

marta: yep will run buckets.

eval-bot: automated summary (first pass): recall@10 delta (quant vs float): en 0.8%, fr -8.9%, jp -9.3%. mean cosine shift: -0.23. silhouette (avg) float=0.42 quant=0.30. flagged: "per-channel quant variance high".

li: FYI try using calibration tables with symmetric minmax vs per-channel abs max. symmetric sometimes keeps center density stable.

marta: plan: 1) run renorm+L2 bucket eval, 2) run Procrustes to isolate rotation vs magnitude loss, 3) retrain small calibration with alpha=0.02 and per-channel symmetric clamp, 4) eva to produce synthetic anchors for FR/JP. i'll post numbers here (~4-6h). assigning: @kevin help with calibration script, @josh add bucket metrics, @eva generate anchors.

kevin: on it. I'll also log the quantization histogram so we can see which dimensions saturate.

eva: starting synthetic anchor job now, ETA ~2h. will push CSV to /shared/evals/synth_anchors/fr_jp_5k.csv

marta: thanks all. if renorm fixes it we can fold renorm into the inference shim for Dedicated until we fix calibration. otherwise we'll have to tweak alpha or clip strategy. will update here when runs finish. :thumbsup:
